newsitem.title: USA: PG&E told to give refund, lift '97 gas rates.
newsitem.headline: PG&E told to give refund, lift '97 gas rates.

text.p: The California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) Tuesday ordered PG&E Corp's Pacific Gas & Electric Co to issue a one-time $25 refund to natural gas customers and to increase gas rates by about 22 percent for the rest of the year.
The refund and rate increase reflect PG&E's over-forecast of both its gas procurement costs and its projected sales for 1996, the CPUC said in a statement.
The refund is to residential and small commercial customers who were over-charged for their gas between March 1996 and February 1997.
The commission said PG&E overestimated the cost of gas for 1996 and then was allowed to set prices based on that overestimation.
However, PG&E also overestimated its gas sales to customers for 1996. The projections did not match sales due mainly to unusually warm weather, the commission said.

The CPUC on Tuesday allowed PG&E to recover the $261 million it under-collected for its transportation account, which is a fixed-cost account based on the company's ability to actually deliver gas to customers.
The increases - about $4 a month for smaller consumers and $21 a month for large commercial customers - will be effective April 1 through the end of 1997.
